To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
triiodothyronin (T3) is a liver mitogen and an antagonist of carcinogenesis.

T3, a hormone that is a ligand of peroxisome-proliferator activated receptors and a strong liver mitogens, induces cell proliferation in liver, and that this effect is associated with a decrease in the number of hepatic nodules and a reduction in the incidence of hepatocellular cancer.

short-term treatment of rats with the thyroid hormone triiodothyrone reduced the size and number (by 70%) of gamma-glutanyl transpeptididase positive hepatic hyperplatic lesions and reduced the number of rats with hepatocellular carcinoma from 100 to 50% and the number of rats developing lung metastasis from 33 to 0%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of thyroid hormone (T3) on hepatocarcinogenesis in rats.
the effects of peroxisome proliferation on the liver.
the role played by cell proliferation induced by peroxisome proliferation in the process of liver carcinogenesis.

T3 is a potent liver mitogen that can be used to induce liver cell proliferation and that, in this model, it is also a liver carcinogen.
